lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Linda, it's Jorge from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After dinner I can walk the dog, she needs it anyway. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: With all the rain I just stayed in.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The rain got in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to walk after every dinner. That's the meal that matters most for your sugar.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Linda, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: 'You have to walk after every dinner' is a directive without permission, undermining autonomy.
Goal of 5 walks set by coach after she said 'Not yet'; not co-created.
Repeated fatigue and 'up and down' feelings were never explored; possible mood or energy concern left unaddressed.
'You've made up your mind' overstated commitment given her hesitance about the schedule.

score.summary: Jorge used some good reflections and affirmations, and Linda voiced real motivation around her diabetes and family. However, he shifted into directing the goal and advice (lines 24 and 46) and did not explore her repeated fatigue or 'up and down' feelings.
strengths: Line 16: complex reflection of ambivalence ('You're weighing it up') was accurate and validating.
Line 33: complex reflection captured her desire to keep moving forward.
Line 42 and 48: checked the plan and summarized it back to her.
coaching_tips: Line 24 and 46: replace directives with a question such as 'What feels like a realistic number of walks for you?' to keep the goal hers.
Line 37: explore the fatigue ('You mentioned being so tired. What's that like for you?') before setting goals.
Line 35: hold off on 'You've made up your mind' when she has just said 'Not yet'; reflect her hesitation instead.
Line 12: ask permission before sharing health information, e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared what I know about walks and blood sugar?'
